I am an old man, 80 years now, but I still work my land. This beans plot I intercrop as we always do here in the North East — the beans bring life back to the soil, so I do not waste money on chemical fertilizer for them. I keep some chickens and a few small ruminants, so I spread their manure on the plot before the rains. The big trouble with cowpea here is the insects — pod-borers and aphids will finish the crop if I do nothing — so I will buy some insecticide from the agro-dealer and spray when the pods are forming. I am too old to do all the weeding and harvesting myself, so my family helps and I hire a few young men for the heavy days.
